scope: Line-by-line review of the origination layer (scripts/originate.py, scripts/build_origination.py, data/origination/aliases.json), the publishing workflow cache, the collector source readers and the session workflows, against official and first-party sources. Every item links the evidence used; nothing here is a probability input.
method: Each item was reproduced locally or on a GitHub runner (runner bundles 38817748368, 38819155716) and checked against the linked source pages and APIs on 2026-10-15 between 22:24Z and 23:05Z. 'fixed' items carry a regression test; 'needs review' items were deliberately not changed by this session.

items.finding: Scheduled publisher runs failed at the build step with KeyError 'source_url' whenever a featured-unresolved fixture was resolved by the Valve-model fallback: scripts/originate.py emitted model inputs without their per-row source_url/snapshot_date while scripts/build.py evidence() renders one linked row per input.
items.handling: originate.py now keeps each input's official source link and snapshot date (already present in the parsed Valve rows). Regression: tests/test_origination.py ModelFallbackRenderTests reproduces the crash through build.evidence().

evidence.detail: Scheduled run 13:26Z failed at 'Reconcile every row, replay every probability and build linked pages'.
Scheduled run 19:53Z failed at the same build step (site frozen on the 12:13Z deployment).
Origination audit annotation: failure 'source_url' with fallback 1080281 resolved by method 'model'.

items.finding: PR #34 made the cache restore path list end with data/origination/ while the save list ends with data/origination/evidence/. actions/cache derives the cache version from the exact path list, so no saved snapshot could ever be restored (outage fallback silently degraded to the old checked-in data), and a matching data/origination/ restore would overlay the reviewed alias registry.
items.handling: Restore list made identical to the save list. Reproduced the toolkit hash locally: old save list = 4a521c6345d7 and new save list = 4ad832c41549 (both match this repository's cache API), PR #34 restore list = 20fc7e29e64c (no cache can match). Regression: tests/test_workflow_cache.py.

evidence.detail: Official README: the cache version is a hash of the compression tool and the cached path list; different versions never match.
getCacheVersion(paths, compressionMethod) hashes paths joined with '|' plus compression method and salt.
Pull request that introduced the mismatched restore list.

items.finding: Production run 38816949473 (22:25Z) published 22 active fixtures with 8 unresolved: only Polymarket, Thunderpick and the Valve model were consulted, and the consensus kept one quote per family, so a second independent market or book would have been discarded.
items.handling: Added Kalshi (CFTC-regulated exchange, officially documented public API, 12-cent spread ceiling) and Bovada (sportsbook public coupon, prematch series moneyline only) with the same exact-name/registry and 60-second start rules; consensus is now one vote per provider. Live runner check 22:45Z: 16 of 22 resolved; Ninjas in Pyjamas vs Team Liquid became a four-provider consensus (Polymarket + Kalshi + Thunderpick + Bovada, NiP 53.3%).

evidence.detail: Annotation 'Public complete-picks counts': active 22, resolved 14, unresolved 8.
Official Kalshi market-data API documentation (public, unauthenticated GET).
Kalshi KXCS2GAME event 'Liquid vs. NIP', Stake Pulse Beat III, originally scheduled Oct 16, 2026 4:00 AM EDT.
Bovada event 32266578 'Ninjas in Pyjamas vs Team Liquid', prematch moneyline 1.769 / 2.00.

items.finding: GitHub delivered the publisher's '17 */4 * * *' schedule on 15 Oct only at 04:39, 13:26 and 19:53 UTC (scheduled-run API), so about half of the slots were dropped and the 04:39 → 13:26 gap was 8.8 hours — above the user's 8-hour bound. Both later runs also failed (C07-01), so the public site stayed on the 12:13Z deployment until the 22:25Z push deploy.
items.handling: Added an offset catch-up schedule ('47 2-22/4 * * *'): 12 slots per day, and any single dropped slot still leaves a refresh within about four hours. Regression: tests/test_workflow_cache.py PublisherScheduleTests (worst single-drop gap ≤ 8 h). Delivery remains best-effort on GitHub's side.

evidence.detail: Official docs: the schedule event can be delayed during high load, including the start of every hour; if load is high enough some queued jobs may be dropped; a workflow can have multiple schedule events.
Scheduled run created 2026-10-15T04:39:02Z (success).
Next scheduled run created 2026-10-15T13:26:23Z (8.8 h later; failed).
Next scheduled run created 2026-10-15T19:53:31Z (failed).
